title: [expo-image-picker] launchCameraAsync doesn’t open the camera on Android after the 2025-09-05 security update
body:
### Minimal reproducible example

https://github.com/reporter/expo-image-picker-test

### Steps to reproduce

After applying the Android security patch 2025-09-05, calling `launchCameraAsync()` from `expo-image-picker` does not show the camera UI immediately.
The camera only appears after the app is backgrounded and then resumed. 


It can be reproduced with the following steps:

- Clone reproducible example
- Run `pnpm install` 
- Run `pnpm run android`
- Tap "Open Camera"


When tapping "Open Camera", logcat outputs the following:

```
Activity                com.example.expoimagepickertest      V  No requestable permission in the request.
```


I’ve confirmed the issue reproduces in the following environments:

- Device: Pixel 9a, Pixel 8, Pixel 7a, Pixel 6
- Android OS: 16
- Security Update: 2025-09-05

comments.body:
Hello, maybe this helps someone until the issue gets fixed. We had the same problems when using `Location.requestForegroundPermissionAsync` and `Location.requestBackgroundPermissionAsync` from `expo-location`. In our case, we managed to kind of work around it by always calling `Location.getForegroundPermissionAsync` or `Location.getBackgroundPermissionAsync` before requesting it. Also, we'd check the `status` and `canAskAgain` values of the response and programatically direct the user to `AppSettings` if needed.

It looks like `getPermission` does resolve even after the initial permission request resolved without the need of sending the app to background so at least it should unblock the normal use cases of most apps which deal with this.

It is not an ideal solution, but maybe it can help others get around the issue.

comments.author: participant55
comments.body:
I'm still able to reproduce this issue on the latest versions, and it appears to be the same behavior described in this issue.

**Environment**

Expo SDK: 54.0.2

expo-image-picker: 17.0.11

React Native: 0.81.5

Android: 16

**Devices tested:**

Pixel 8 Pro

Pixel 7a

**Observed behavior**

Calling ImagePicker.launchCameraAsync() does not open the camera immediately.

The interesting part is that the camera launch appears to be deferred until the application's Activity goes through another lifecycle transition.

**For example:**

Tap Use Camera.

launchCameraAsync() is called.

Nothing happens (camera does not open).

Put the app into the background (e.g. open another app from Recents) and then return.

The camera opens automatically.

The same behavior also occurs after locking and unlocking the device.

If the user taps the camera button multiple times while nothing is happening, multiple camera activities are queued and are launched one after another once the lifecycle transition occurs.

**Additional observations**

Camera permission is already granted before calling launchCameraAsync(), so this does not appear to be related to the permission request flow.

Reproduced consistently on both Pixel 7a and Pixel 8 Pro.

I verified the same flow on other Android devices and could not reproduce the issue there.

The issue persists even after killing and reopening the app.

Another commenter in this thread mentioned that triggering a lifecycle change using Linking.openURL(<app-scheme>://)works as a temporary workaround. That workaround also matches the behavior I'm observing, which further suggests that the camera launch is waiting for an Activity lifecycle transition before being executed.

**Relevant logcat**

When launchCameraAsync() is invoked, Expo reaches the Activity Result launcher:

expo.modules.kotlin.activityresult.AppContextActivityResultRegistry.onLaunch(AppContextActivityResultRegistry.kt:148)
expo.modules.kotlin.activityresult.AppContextActivityResultLauncher.launch(AppContextActivityResultLauncher.kt:26)
expo.modules.imagepicker.ImagePickerModule$definition$1$5$1.invokeSuspend(ImagePickerModule.kt:79)
expo.modules.imagepicker.ImagePickerModule$launchPicker$2.invokeSuspend(ImagePickerModule.kt:243)
Android also logs the following warnings immediately before the camera activity is started:

Implicit URI read grant for ImageCapture action will be discontinued from Android 18 onwards.
Implicit URI write grant for ImageCapture action will be discontinued from Android 18 onwards.
The camera activity is eventually launched by Android:

ActivityTaskManager: START u0 {act=android.media.action.IMAGE_CAPTURE ...}
cmp=com.google.android.GoogleCamera/com.android.camera.activity.CaptureActivity
Immediately afterwards, React Native reports the expected lifecycle callbacks:

ReactHost.onUserLeaveHint(activity)
ReactHost.onHostPause(activity)
ReactContext.onHostPause()
From my testing, this looks like the intent to launch the camera is created successfully, but on Pixel devices running Android 16 it is not presented until another Activity lifecycle transition occurs.

If there's any additional logging or a minimal reproduction that would help, I'd be happy to provide it.
